Centurion

A flexible and extensible command framework for Roblox

[![CI status][ci-badge]][ci-url] [![npm latest version][npm-latest-badge]][npm-latest-url] [![MIT License][license-badge]][license-url] [npm-latest-badge]: https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@rbxts/centurion.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=npm [npm-latest-url]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rbxts/centurion/v/latest [ci-badge]: https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/paradoxuum/centurion/ci.yml?style=for-the-badge&branch=main&logo=github [ci-url]: https://github.com/paradoxuum/centurion/actions/workflows/ci.yml [license-badge]: https://img.shields.io/github/license/paradoxuum/centurion?style=for-the-badge [license-url]: https://github.com/paradoxuum/centurion/blob/main/LICENSE.md [📖 **Documentation →**](https://centurion.paradoxum.dev/)
## ✨ Features - 🌙 **Luau and roblox-ts.** Written in Luau with full TypeScript typings, and available on both Wally and npm. - ✏️ **Simple to define.** Register commands with a plain table, or use decorators and classes in roblox-ts. - 🧩 **Typed arguments.** Built-in types for players, teams, numbers, colors, durations, vectors and more, with optional, multi-value and rest arguments. Register your own types with custom suggestions. - 🔐 **Guards and permissions.** Guard commands with reusable checks, and control access with inheritable roles and permissions. - 🔄 **Client-server sync.** Players only receive the commands they're allowed to run, and stay up to date as commands or roles change. - 💻 **Optional terminal UI.** A clean console with suggestions, fuzzy matching, tab completion, syntax highlighting and history. Use it as-is, theme it, or build your own. ## 📦 Installation ```toml # wally.toml [dependencies] centurion = "paradoxuum/centurion@2.0.0" centurion-ui = "paradoxuum/centurion-ui@2.0.0" ``` ```bash # roblox-ts npm install @rbxts/centurion @rbxts/centurion-ui ``` See the [documentation](https://centurion.paradoxum.dev/) to get started. ## 💖 Attributions - [🍀 Charm](https://github.com/littensy/charm): Inspiration for command syncing - [💻 Conch](https://github.com/alicesaidhi/conch): UI utility components and text box state handling - [🌿 Vide](https://github.com/centau/vide): Reactive UI library powering the terminal UI ---

local argument = require("./argument")
local context = require("./context")
local guard = require("./guard")
local log = require("./log")
local permission = require("./permission")
local services = require("./services")
local types = require("./types")

local commands: types.CommandMap = {}

type RegisterCallback = (name: string, command: types.Command<unknown>) -> ()

local on_register_callbacks: { RegisterCallback } = {}
local on_unregister_callbacks: { RegisterCallback } = {}
local on_execute_callbacks: { (ctx: types.ExecutionContext) -> () } = {}
local on_fail_callbacks: { (ctx: types.ExecutionContext, reason: types.FailReason) -> () } = {}

type NetworkHandler = (command: string, args: { string }?, input: string?) -> types.ExecutionContext

local network_handler: NetworkHandler?

local function set_network_handler(callback: NetworkHandler)
	network_handler = callback
end

local function notify(event: string, listeners: { (...any) -> () }, ctx: types.ExecutionContext, ...: any)
	for _, callback in table.clone(listeners) do
		local ok, err = xpcall(callback :: any, log.capture, ctx, ...)
		if not ok then
			local caught: log.CaughtError = err
			log.error(`{event} listener failed for '{ctx.input}': {caught.message}`, {
				executor = ctx.executor,
				command = ctx.command,
				input = ctx.input,
				traceback = caught.traceback,
			})
		end
	end
end

local function fail(ctx: types.ExecutionContext, reason: types.FailReason): types.ExecutionContext
	notify("on_command_fail", on_fail_callbacks :: any, ctx, reason)
	return ctx
end

local function call_guard(ctx: types.ExecutionContext, name: string, callback: (ctx: types.ExecutionContext) -> boolean)
	local result, value = xpcall(callback :: any, log.capture, ctx)
	if not result then
		local caught: log.CaughtError = value
		log.error(`Guard execution failed for '{name}': {caught.message}`, {
			executor = ctx.executor,
			command = ctx.command,
			input = ctx.input,
			guard = name,
			traceback = caught.traceback,
		})
		ctx.error("Failed to execute command.")
		return false
	end

	if value == true then
		return true
	end

	if value ~= false then
		log.warn(`Guard '{name}' returned {typeof(value)} instead of a boolean. Did you forget to return true?`, {
			executor = ctx.executor,
			command = ctx.command,
			input = ctx.input,
			guard = name,
		})
	end

	if not ctx.response then
		ctx.error("You cannot execute this command.")
	end

	return false
end

local function check_access(ctx: types.ExecutionContext, command: types.Command<unknown>?): types.FailReason?
	if command == nil or commands[ctx.command] ~= command then
		ctx.error("Unknown command")
		return "unknown"
	end

	if not permission.can_execute(ctx.executor, command) then
		if permission.options.hide then
			ctx.error("Unknown command")
		else
			ctx.error("You do not have permission to execute this command.")
		end

		return "permission"
	end

	return nil
end

-- `input` is the raw, untokenized string the executor submitted. Pass it
-- whenever it's available so that `ctx.input` keeps the original quoting.
local function execute(executor: Player, name: string, args: { string }?, input: string?): types.ExecutionContext
	args = args or {}
	local ctx = context(executor, name, args, input)

	local command = commands[name]
	local denied: types.FailReason? = check_access(ctx, command)
	if denied then
		return fail(ctx, denied)
	end

	if not command.callback then
		assert(network_handler, "Network handler must be set before server command execution on the client.")
		return network_handler(name, args, input)
	end

	-- clone so that a guard removing itself (or another global
	-- guard) mid-loop can't cause the next one to be skipped
	for i, v in table.clone(guard.global_guards) do
		if not call_guard(ctx, `global guard #{i}`, v) then
			return fail(ctx, "guard")
		end
	end

	if command.guards then
		for i, cmd_guard in command.guards do
			if type(cmd_guard) ~= "string" then
				if not call_guard(ctx, `guard #{i}`, cmd_guard :: types.Guard) then
					return fail(ctx, "guard")
				end
				continue
			end

			-- registration checks that named guards exist, but one can be
			-- unregistered afterwards. fail closed rather than skip it
			local guard_callback = guard.guards[cmd_guard]
			if not guard_callback then
				log.warn(`Guard '{cmd_guard}' used by command '{name}' is not registered.`, {
					executor = executor,
					command = name,
					input = ctx.input,
					guard = cmd_guard,
				})
				ctx.error("Failed to execute command.")
				return fail(ctx, "guard")
			end

			if not call_guard(ctx, cmd_guard, guard_callback) then
				return fail(ctx, "guard")
			end
		end
	end

	-- always transform, even with no declared arguments, so that commands
	-- taking none still reject extra input
	local command_args: { types.Argument } = if command.arguments
		then { command.arguments() } :: { types.Argument }
		else {}

	-- transforms are user code too, so a throwing one is handled like a
	-- throwing guard or callback rather than escaping to the network handler
	local transformed, res = xpcall(argument.transform :: any, log.capture, executor, args, command_args)
	if not transformed then
		local caught: log.CaughtError = res
		log.error(`Failed to transform arguments for '{ctx.input}': {caught.message}`, {
			executor = executor,
			command = name,
			input = ctx.input,
			traceback = caught.traceback,
		})
		ctx.error("Failed to execute command.")
		return fail(ctx, "arguments")
	end

	if not res.success then
		ctx.error(res.error)
		return fail(ctx, "arguments")
	end

	-- guards and transforms can yield, so the executor's roles may have been revoked,
	-- or the command replaced, since the previous check
	denied = check_access(ctx, command)
	if denied then
		return fail(ctx, denied)
	end

	-- unpack up to the declared argument count so that omitted optional
	-- arguments don't truncate the ones after them
	local success, value = xpcall(command.callback :: any, log.capture, ctx, unpack(res.value, 1, #command_args))
	if not success then
		local caught: log.CaughtError = value
		log.error(`Failed to execute '{ctx.input}': {caught.message}`, {
			executor = executor,
			command = name,
			input = ctx.input,
			traceback = caught.traceback,
		})
		ctx.error("Failed to execute command.")
		return fail(ctx, "callback")
	end

	if type(value) == "string" then
		ctx.reply(value)
	end

	notify("on_command_execute", on_execute_callbacks :: any, ctx)
	return ctx
end

local function check_arity(name: string, callback: (...any) -> any, declared: number, offset: number)
	local nparams, is_vararg = debug.info(callback, "a")

	if is_vararg or nparams == 0 then
		return
	end

	local takes = (nparams :: number) - offset
	if takes ~= declared then
		log.warn(
			`Command '{name}' declares {declared} {declared == 1 and "argument" or "arguments"} but its callback takes {takes}.`,
			{ command = name }
		)
	end
end

local function validate_command(name: string, command: types.Command<unknown>)
	local args: { types.Argument } = command.arguments and { command.arguments() } :: { types.Argument } or {}

	if command.guards then
		for _, cmd_guard in command.guards do
			if type(cmd_guard) == "string" then
				assert(guard.guards[cmd_guard], `Guard '{cmd_guard}' used by command '{name}' is not registered.`)
			end
		end
	end

	local has_roles = command.roles ~= nil and #command.roles > 0
	local has_permissions = command.permissions ~= nil and #command.permissions > 0

	-- roles only exist on the server, so a restricted command registered on the
	-- client could never pass can_execute. synced commands have these stripped
	if (has_roles or has_permissions) and services.RunService:IsRunning() and not services.RunService:IsServer() then
		error(
			`Command '{name}' restricts roles or permissions, which are only checked on the server. Register it on the server instead.`
		)
	end

	if command.roles then
		for _, role_name in command.roles do
			assert(permission.roles[role_name], `Role '{role_name}' used by command '{name}' is not registered.`)
		end
	end

	local optional_found = false
	for i, arg in args do
		assert(argument.types[arg.type], `Argument type '{arg.type}' for argument '{arg.name}' is not registered.`)

		if arg.optional then
			optional_found = true
		elseif optional_found then
			error(`Required argument '{arg.name}' cannot follow an optional argument.`)
		end

		local n = arg.num_args
		if n == "rest" then
			if i ~= #args then
				error(`Argument '{arg.name}' is declared as 'rest' but is not the last argument.`)
			end
		elseif n ~= nil and (type(n) ~= "number" or n < 1 or n % 1 ~= 0) then
			error(`Argument '{arg.name}' has an invalid num_args: {n}. Expected a whole number of at least 1.`)
		end
	end

	-- a command synced from the server has no callback on the client, since it
	-- executes over the network handler instead
	if command.callback then
		check_arity(name, command.callback :: any, #args, 1)
	end
end

local function register<T...>(name: string | { string }, command: types.Command<T...>)
	local names: { string } = typeof(name) == "string" and { name } or (name :: { string })

	validate_command(names[1], command :: types.Command<unknown>)

	for _, v in names do
		assert(commands[v] == nil, "Command with name '" .. v .. "' is already registered.")
	end

	for _, v in names do
		commands[v] = command :: any
	end

	-- once per name, so listeners see every alias
	for _, v in names do
		for _, callback in table.clone(on_register_callbacks) do
			callback(v, command :: types.Command<unknown>)
		end
	end
end

local function command<T...>(name: string | { string }, definition: types.CommandDefinition<T...>): types.CommandBuilder<T...>
	return {
		callback = function(_self, callback)
			local cmd = table.clone(definition) :: any
			cmd.callback = callback
			register(name, cmd :: types.Command<T...>)
		end,
	}
end

local function unregister(name: string)
	assert(commands[name] ~= nil, "Command with name '" .. name .. "' is not registered.")

	local cmd_definition = commands[name]

	-- unregistering any name removes the command's aliases too
	local names: { string } = {}
	for k, v in commands do
		if cmd_definition == v then
			table.insert(names, k)
		end
	end
	table.sort(names)

	for _, v in names do
		commands[v] = nil
	end

	for _, v in names do
		for _, callback in table.clone(on_unregister_callbacks) do
			callback(v, cmd_definition :: types.Command<unknown>)
		end
	end
end

local function on_register(callback: RegisterCallback)
	table.insert(on_register_callbacks, callback)

	return function()
		local index = table.find(on_register_callbacks, callback)
		if index then
			table.remove(on_register_callbacks, index)
		end
	end
end

local function on_unregister(callback: RegisterCallback)
	table.insert(on_unregister_callbacks, callback)

	return function()
		local index = table.find(on_unregister_callbacks, callback)
		if index then
			table.remove(on_unregister_callbacks, index)
		end
	end
end

local function on_execute(callback: (ctx: types.ExecutionContext) -> ())
	table.insert(on_execute_callbacks, callback)

	return function()
		local index = table.find(on_execute_callbacks, callback)
		if index then
			table.remove(on_execute_callbacks, index)
		end
	end
end

local function on_fail(callback: (ctx: types.ExecutionContext, reason: types.FailReason) -> ())
	table.insert(on_fail_callbacks, callback)

	return function()
		local index = table.find(on_fail_callbacks, callback)
		if index then
			table.remove(on_fail_callbacks, index)
		end
	end
end

return {
	set_network_handler = set_network_handler,
	execute = execute,
	register = register,
	command = command,
	unregister = unregister,
	on_register = on_register,
	on_unregister = on_unregister,
	on_execute = on_execute,
	on_fail = on_fail,
	commands = commands,
	check_arity = check_arity,
}

local types = require("./types")

local function context(executor: Player, command: string, args: { string }, input: string?): types.ExecutionContext
	local ctx = {
		executor = executor,
		command = command,
		input = input or (command .. (#args > 0 and (" " .. table.concat(args, " ")) or "")),
		arguments = args,
	} :: types.ExecutionContext

	-- the response is serialized after the handler returns, where a non-string
	-- message would fail and leave the client waiting, so coerce it here
	ctx.reply = function(message: string)
		ctx.response = {
			success = true,
			message = tostring(message),
			timestamp = os.time(),
		}
	end

	ctx.error = function(message: string)
		ctx.response = {
			success = false,
			message = tostring(message),
			timestamp = os.time(),
		}
	end

	return ctx
end

return context

local types = require("./types")

local guards = {}
local global_guards: { types.Guard } = {}

local function register(name: string, guard: types.Guard)
	assert(guards[name] == nil, "Guard with name '" .. name .. "' already exists.")

	guards[name] = guard
end

local function unregister(name: string)
	assert(guards[name] ~= nil, "Guard with name '" .. name .. "' is not registered.")

	guards[name] = nil
end

-- returns a function that removes the guard again. calling it more than once
-- does nothing.
local function add_global(guard: types.Guard): () -> ()
	table.insert(global_guards, guard)

	local removed = false
	return function()
		if removed then
			return
		end
		removed = true

		local index = table.find(global_guards, guard)
		if index then
			table.remove(global_guards, index)
		end
	end
end

return {
	register = register,
	unregister = unregister,
	add_global = add_global,
	guards = guards,
	global_guards = global_guards,
}

local services = require("./services")

-- limits on remote command execution. everything sent over the `Execute`
-- remote is client-controlled, so each player gets a token bucket and the
-- request is size-checked before it reaches the registry
export type ExecuteLimits = {
	rate: number?,
	burst: number?,
	max_args: number?,
	max_arg_length: number?,
	max_input_length: number?,
}

type Bucket = {
	tokens: number,
	updated: number,
}

local opts = {
	rate = 2,
	-- how many commands can be executed in quick succession
	burst = 10,
	max_args = 32,
	max_arg_length = 256,
	max_input_length = 1024,
}

local buckets: { [Player]: Bucket } = {}
local player_removing_connection: RBXScriptConnection?

local limit = {
	-- replaceable so tests can control time
	clock = os.clock,
}

-- buckets are cleared when a player leaves. this is connected on first use
-- rather than at load so that requiring this module never touches the datamodel
local function track_players()
	if player_removing_connection then
		return
	end

	player_removing_connection = services.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		buckets[player] = nil
	end)
end

local function take_token(player: Player): boolean
	track_players()

	local now = limit.clock()
	local bucket = buckets[player]
	if bucket then
		bucket.tokens = math.min(opts.burst, bucket.tokens + (now - bucket.updated) * opts.rate)
		bucket.updated = now
	else
		bucket = { tokens = opts.burst, updated = now }
		buckets[player] = bucket
	end

	if bucket.tokens < 1 then
		return false
	end

	bucket.tokens -= 1
	return true
end

function limit.check_name(name: string): boolean
	return #name <= opts.max_arg_length
end

function limit.check(player: Player, name: string, args: { string }?, input: string?): string?
	if not take_token(player) then
		return "You're running commands too quickly. Try again in a moment."
	end

	if not limit.check_name(name) then
		return `Command name is too long (max {opts.max_arg_length} characters).`
	end

	if args then
		if #args > opts.max_args then
			return `Too many arguments (max {opts.max_args}).`
		end

		for _, arg in args do
			if #arg > opts.max_arg_length then
				return `Argument is too long (max {opts.max_arg_length} characters).`
			end
		end
	end

	if input and #input > opts.max_input_length then
		return `Input is too long (max {opts.max_input_length} characters).`
	end

	return nil
end

function limit.set_options(options: ExecuteLimits)
	local current = opts :: { [string]: number }
	for key, value in options :: { [string]: number } do
		assert(
			current[key] ~= nil,
			`Unknown execute limit '{key}'. Expected rate, burst, max_args, max_arg_length or max_input_length.`
		)
		assert(type(value) == "number" and value > 0, `Execute limit '{key}' must be a positive number.`)
		current[key] = value
	end
end

function limit.reset(player: Player?)
	if player then
		buckets[player] = nil
	else
		table.clear(buckets)
	end
end

return limit

-- everything the core reports goes through here so that it can be routed to a
-- logging or analytics service with `set_logger`.
--
-- "error" is for exceptions thrown by user code (guards and callbacks) and
-- carries a traceback. "warn" is for misconfiguration that doesn't stop the
-- core from working.

export type LogLevel = "warn" | "error"

export type LogInfo = {
	executor: Player?,
	command: string?,
	input: string?,
	guard: string?,
	traceback: string?,
}

export type Logger = (level: LogLevel, message: string, info: LogInfo) -> ()

export type CaughtError = {
	message: string,
	traceback: string,
}

local function default_logger(_level: LogLevel, message: string, info: LogInfo)
	if info.traceback then
		warn(`{message}\n{info.traceback}`)
	else
		warn(message)
	end
end

local logger: Logger = default_logger

local function set_logger(callback: Logger?)
	logger = callback or default_logger
end

local function log(level: LogLevel, message: string, info: LogInfo?)
	local log_info: LogInfo = info or {}

	-- a broken logger shouldn't take down whatever was being reported, so
	-- fall back to the default rather than letting the error propagate
	local ok, err = pcall(logger, level, message, log_info)
	if not ok then
		default_logger("warn", `Logger failed: {err}`, {})
		default_logger(level, message, log_info)
	end
end

-- an `xpcall` handler. it runs where the error was thrown, so the traceback
-- still points into the code that threw rather than at the `xpcall`.
local function capture(err: unknown): CaughtError
	local traceback = string.gsub(debug.traceback(nil, 2), "\n$", "")

	return {
		message = tostring(err),
		traceback = traceback,
	}
end

return {
	set_logger = set_logger,
	warn = function(message: string, info: LogInfo?)
		log("warn", message, info)
	end,
	error = function(message: string, info: LogInfo?)
		log("error", message, info)
	end,
	capture = capture,
}

export type ParseResult = {
	tokens: { Token },
	unclosed_quote: boolean,
}

export type Token = {
	span: vector,
	text: string,
	quoted: boolean,
}

local function parse_escaped_char(c: string): string
	if c == "n" then
		return "\n"
	elseif c == "t" then
		return "\t"
	elseif c == "r" then
		return "\r"
	elseif c == "\\" then
		return "\\"
	elseif c == '"' then
		return '"'
	elseif c == "'" then
		return "'"
	end

	return c
end

local function parse(text: string, split_char: string): ParseResult
	local tokens: { Token } = {}

	local start = nil
	local escaped = false
	local quote_char: string?
	local quoted = false
	local current = ""

	for i = 1, #text do
		local c = text:sub(i, i)

		if escaped then
			if start == nil then
				start = i - 1
			end

			current = current .. parse_escaped_char(c)
			escaped = false
			continue
		end

		if c == "\\" then
			escaped = true
			continue
		end

		if (c == '"' or c == "'") and not quote_char then
			quote_char = c
			quoted = true
			if start == nil then
				start = i
			end
			continue
		end

		if c == quote_char then
			quote_char = nil
			continue
		end

		if not quote_char and c == split_char then
			if start ~= nil then
				table.insert(tokens, {
					span = vector.create(start, i - 1, 0),
					text = current,
					quoted = quoted,
				})
				start = nil
				current = ""
				quoted = false
			end
			continue
		end

		if start == nil then
			start = i
		end

		current = current .. c
	end

	if start ~= nil then
		table.insert(tokens, {
			span = vector.create(start, #text, 0),
			text = current,
			quoted = quoted,
		})
	end

	return {
		tokens = tokens,
		unclosed_quote = quote_char ~= nil,
	}
end

return parse

local services = require("./services")
local types = require("./types")

type PermissionOptions = {
	hide: boolean?,
	default_roles: { string }?,
	deny_unrestricted: boolean?,
}

local roles: { [string]: types.PermissionRole } = {}
local players: { [number]: { string } } = {}
local opts: PermissionOptions = {
	hide = true,
	deny_unrestricted = false,
}
local changed_callbacks: { [number]: { (roles: { string }) -> () } } = {}
local options_callbacks: { (options: PermissionOptions) -> () } = {}
local role_callbacks: { (name: string) -> () } = {}

local player_removing_connection: RBXScriptConnection?

-- per-player state is cleared when they leave. this is connected on first use
-- rather than at load so that requiring this module never touches the datamodel
local function track_players()
	if player_removing_connection then
		return
	end

	player_removing_connection = services.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		players[player.UserId] = nil
		changed_callbacks[player.UserId] = nil
	end)
end

export type RoleOptions = {
	permissions: { string }?,
	inherits: { string }?,
}

type Resolved = { roles: { [string]: true }, permissions: { [string]: true } }

local resolved: { [string]: Resolved } = {}

-- what a role grants once its inherited roles are included. the roles it
-- inherits from must already be resolved
local function resolve(name: string): Resolved
	local role = roles[name]
	local granted: Resolved = {
		roles = { [name] = true },
		permissions = {},
	}

	for perm in role.permissions do
		granted.permissions[perm] = true
	end

	for _, parent_name in role.inherits do
		local parent = resolved[parent_name]
		for role_name in parent.roles do
			granted.roles[role_name] = true
		end
		for perm in parent.permissions do
			granted.permissions[perm] = true
		end
	end

	return granted
end

local function validate_inherits(name: string, inherits: { string })
	for _, parent_name in inherits do
		local parent = resolved[parent_name]
		assert(parent, `Role '{name}' inherits from '{parent_name}', which is not registered.`)

		-- a role can only already be inherited by its parent when editing it
		if parent.roles[name] then
			error(`Role '{name}' can't inherit from '{parent_name}', which already inherits from it.`)
		end
	end
end

local function permission_set(permissions: { string }?): { [string]: boolean }
	local set = {}
	if permissions then
		for _, perm in permissions do
			set[perm] = true
		end
	end
	return set
end

local function create_role(name: string, options: RoleOptions?)
	assert(roles[name] == nil, `Role '{name}' is already registered.`)

	local inherits = if options and options.inherits then table.clone(options.inherits) else {}
	validate_inherits(name, inherits)

	roles[name] = {
		name = name,
		permissions = permission_set(options and options.permissions),
		inherits = inherits,
	}
	resolved[name] = resolve(name)
end

local function update_role(name: string, options: RoleOptions)
	local role = roles[name]
	assert(role ~= nil, `Role '{name}' is not registered.`)

	local inherits = if options.inherits then table.clone(options.inherits) else role.inherits
	validate_inherits(name, inherits)

	-- the role and every role inheriting from it, found before the edit. the
	-- edit only changes this role's parents, so the set stays the same after
	local affected: { [string]: true } = {}
	for other_name, granted in resolved do
		if granted.roles[name] then
			affected[other_name] = true
		end
	end

	roles[name] = {
		name = name,
		permissions = if options.permissions then permission_set(options.permissions) else role.permissions,
		inherits = inherits,
	}

	-- re-resolve parents before the roles inheriting from them
	local done: { [string]: true } = {}
	local function visit(role_name: string)
		if done[role_name] then
			return
		end
		done[role_name] = true

		for _, parent_name in roles[role_name].inherits do
			if affected[parent_name] then
				visit(parent_name)
			end
		end
		resolved[role_name] = resolve(role_name)
	end

	for role_name in affected do
		visit(role_name)
	end

	for _, callback in table.clone(role_callbacks) do
		callback(name)
	end
end

local function assign(user_id: number, role_names: { string })
	players[user_id] = table.clone(role_names)

	local callbacks = changed_callbacks[user_id]
	if callbacks then
		for _, callback in table.clone(callbacks) do
			callback(table.clone(role_names))
		end
	end
end

local function delete_role(name: string)
	assert(roles[name] ~= nil, `Role '{name}' is not registered.`)

	for other_name, other in roles do
		if table.find(other.inherits, name) then
			error(`Role '{name}' is inherited by '{other_name}'. Delete that role first.`)
		end
	end

	if opts.default_roles and table.find(opts.default_roles, name) then
		error(`Role '{name}' is a default role. Remove it from the default roles first.`)
	end

	roles[name] = nil
	resolved[name] = nil

	for user_id, assigned in table.clone(players) do
		local index = table.find(assigned, name)
		if index then
			local new_roles = table.clone(assigned)
			table.remove(new_roles, index)
			assign(user_id, new_roles)
		end
	end
end

local function get_roles(player: Player): { string }
	local current = players[player.UserId]
	return if current then table.clone(current) else {}
end

local function set_roles(player: Player, role_names: { string })
	for _, role_name in role_names do
		if not roles[role_name] then
			error("Role '" .. role_name .. "' does not exist.")
		end
	end

	if player.Parent ~= services.Players then
		return
	end

	track_players()
	assign(player.UserId, role_names)
end

local function add_roles(player: Player, ...: string)
	local new_roles = players[player.UserId] and table.clone(players[player.UserId]) or {}
	for _, role_name in { ... } do
		if table.find(new_roles, role_name) then
			continue
		end
		table.insert(new_roles, role_name)
	end
	set_roles(player, new_roles)
end

local function remove_roles(player: Player, ...: string)
	local current_roles = players[player.UserId]
	if not current_roles then
		return
	end

	local role_names = { ... }
	local new_roles: { string } = {}
	for _, role_name in current_roles do
		if table.find(role_names, role_name) then
			continue
		end
		table.insert(new_roles, role_name)
	end
	set_roles(player, new_roles)
end

-- calls `check` with what each of the player's roles grants, assigned roles
-- first and then default roles, until it returns true
local function any_granted(player: Player, check: (granted: Resolved) -> boolean): boolean
	local assigned = players[player.UserId]
	if assigned then
		for _, role_name in assigned do
			local granted = resolved[role_name]
			if granted and check(granted) then
				return true
			end
		end
	end

	if opts.default_roles then
		for _, role_name in opts.default_roles do
			local granted = resolved[role_name]
			if granted and check(granted) then
				return true
			end
		end
	end

	return false
end

local function has_permission(player: Player, permission: string): boolean
	if not services.RunService:IsRunning() then
		return true
	end

	return any_granted(player, function(granted)
		return granted.permissions[permission] == true
	end)
end

local function can_execute(player: Player, command: types.Command<unknown>): boolean
	if not services.RunService:IsRunning() then
		return true
	end

	local required_roles = command.roles or {}
	local required_permissions = command.permissions or {}
	-- only the server denies these, since commands registered on the client
	-- can't have roles and synced commands have theirs stripped
	if #required_roles == 0 and #required_permissions == 0 then
		return not (opts.deny_unrestricted and services.RunService:IsServer())
	end

	return any_granted(player, function(granted)
		for _, role_name in required_roles do
			if granted.roles[role_name] then
				return true
			end
		end

		for _, permission in required_permissions do
			if granted.permissions[permission] then
				return true
			end
		end

		return false
	end)
end

local function set_permission_options(options: PermissionOptions)
	if options.hide ~= nil then
		opts.hide = options.hide
	end

	if options.deny_unrestricted ~= nil then
		opts.deny_unrestricted = options.deny_unrestricted
	end

	-- default roles aren't copied into each player's roles, they're checked
	-- alongside them. so set_roles can't remove them and there's no PlayerAdded
	-- ordering to get wrong
	if options.default_roles ~= nil then
		for _, role_name in options.default_roles do
			if not roles[role_name] then
				error("Role '" .. role_name .. "' does not exist.")
			end
		end
		opts.default_roles = table.clone(options.default_roles)
	end

	for _, callback in table.clone(options_callbacks) do
		callback(opts)
	end
end

local function on_roles_changed(player: Player, callback: (roles: { string }) -> ())
	track_players()

	if not changed_callbacks[player.UserId] then
		changed_callbacks[player.UserId] = {}
	end
	table.insert(changed_callbacks[player.UserId], callback)

	return function()
		local callbacks = changed_callbacks[player.UserId]
		if not callbacks then
			return
		end

		local index = table.find(callbacks, callback)
		if index then
			table.remove(callbacks, index)
		end

		if #callbacks == 0 then
			changed_callbacks[player.UserId] = nil
		end
	end
end

local function on_options_changed(callback: (options: PermissionOptions) -> ())
	table.insert(options_callbacks, callback)
	return function()
		local index = table.find(options_callbacks, callback)
		if index then
			table.remove(options_callbacks, index)
		end
	end
end

-- fires when a role is edited, which can change what any player is granted
local function on_role_updated(callback: (name: string) -> ())
	table.insert(role_callbacks, callback)
	return function()
		local index = table.find(role_callbacks, callback)
		if index then
			table.remove(role_callbacks, index)
		end
	end
end

return {
	create_role = create_role,
	update_role = update_role,
	delete_role = delete_role,
	get_roles = get_roles,
	set_roles = set_roles,
	add_roles = add_roles,
	remove_roles = remove_roles,
	can_execute = can_execute,
	has_permission = has_permission,
	set_permission_options = set_permission_options,
	on_roles_changed = on_roles_changed,
	on_options_changed = on_options_changed,
	on_role_updated = on_role_updated,
	roles = roles,
	options = opts,
}

local types = require("./types")

export type Resolution = {
	-- the resolved command, or nil if the input doesn't name one
	name: string?,
	-- index of the last token making up the command name, 0 if unresolved
	name_end: number,
	args: { string },
	tokens: { parse.Token },
	unclosed_quote: boolean,
}

--[[
	Resolves command input into a registered command name and its arguments.

	Command names may contain spaces, so the longest registered name wins:
	with both `roles` and `roles get` registered, `roles get Player` resolves to
	`roles get`.

	A quoted token is literal text and can never form part of a
	name, so `roles "get"` resolves to `roles` with `get` as its argument.
]]
local function resolve(commands: types.CommandMap, text: string): Resolution
	local parse_result = parse(text, " ")
	local tokens = parse_result.tokens

	local name: string? = nil
	local name_end = 0

	local candidate = {}
	for i, token in tokens do
		if token.quoted then
			break
		end

		table.insert(candidate, token.text)

		local candidate_name = table.concat(candidate, " ")
		if commands[candidate_name] then
			name = candidate_name
			name_end = i
		end
	end

	local args = {}
	for i = name_end + 1, #tokens do
		local token = tokens[i]
		table.insert(args, text:sub(token.span.x, token.span.y))
	end

	return {
		name = name,
		name_end = name_end,
		args = args,
		tokens = tokens,
		unclosed_quote = parse_result.unclosed_quote,
	}
end

return resolve

local command = require("./command")
local context = require("./context")
local limit = require("./limit")
local log = require("./log")
local parse = require("./parse")
local permission = require("./permission")
local services = require("./services")
local types = require("./types")

type CommandState = {
	kind: "command",
	data: types.Command<unknown>,
}

type NetworkedState = CommandState | { kind: "none" }

type NetworkedMap = { [string]: NetworkedState }

export type SyncPayload =
	{
		type: "init",
		data: NetworkedMap,
	}
	| {
		type: "patch",
		data: NetworkedMap,
	}

export type SyncCallback = (player: Player, payload: SyncPayload) -> ()

local function client()
	local hydrated = false
	local synced: types.CommandMap = {}

	local function process_cmd(cmd): any
		local args: { any }? = cmd.arguments
		if not args then
			return cmd
		end

		local processed = table.clone(cmd)
		processed.arguments = function()
			return table.unpack(args)
		end :: any

		return processed
	end

	local function remove(key: string)
		local cmd = synced[key]
		if cmd == nil then
			return
		end

		synced[key] = nil
		if command.commands[key] == cmd then
			command.unregister(key)
		end
	end

	local function add(key: string, data: types.Command<unknown>)
		remove(key)

		if command.commands[key] ~= nil then
			log.warn(`Command '{key}' is already registered on the client, so the server's command was not synced.`, {
				command = key,
			})
			return
		end

		-- one command failing to register (e.g. an argument type that only
		-- exists on the server) shouldn't stop the rest of the payload
		local cmd = process_cmd(data)
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			command.register(key, cmd)
		end)
		if not ok then
			log.warn(`Failed to sync command '{key}': {err}`, { command = key })
			return
		end

		synced[key] = cmd
	end

	local function hydrate(state: NetworkedMap)
		hydrated = true

		for key in synced do
			if state[key] == nil then
				remove(key)
			end
		end

		for key, value in state do
			if value.kind == "command" then
				add(key, value.data)
			end
		end
	end

	local function apply(data: NetworkedMap)
		for key, value in data do
			if value.kind == "command" then
				add(key, value.data)
			else
				remove(key)
			end
		end
	end

	local function sync(...)
		for index = 1, select("#", ...) do
			local payload: SyncPayload = select(index, ...)

			if payload.type == "init" then
				hydrate(payload.data)
			elseif hydrated then
				apply(payload.data)
			end
		end
	end

	return {
		sync = sync,
	}
end

-- only what the client needs: the callback, guards and permissions stay on the
-- server, and the client executes over the network handler instead
local function serialize(cmd: types.Command<unknown>): NetworkedState
	return {
		kind = "command",
		data = {
			description = cmd.description,
			arguments = if cmd.arguments then { cmd.arguments() } else nil,
		} :: any,
	}
end

type PlayerState = {
	-- the commands this player can currently see, as last sent to them
	visible: types.CommandMap,
	hydrated: boolean,
	dirty: boolean,
	disconnect: () -> (),
}

local function server()
	local players: { [Player]: PlayerState } = {}
	local send: SyncCallback?

	local registry: types.CommandMap = {}
	local registry_dirty = false
	local options_dirty = false

	-- a command only changes by being registered again, so it can be
	-- serialized once and the result reused for every player and every tick
	local serialized: { [types.Command<unknown>]: NetworkedState } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" }) :: any

	local function get_serialized(cmd: types.Command<unknown>): NetworkedState
		local state = serialized[cmd]
		if state == nil then
			state = serialize(cmd)
			serialized[cmd] = state
		end
		return state
	end

	local function is_visible(player: Player, cmd: types.Command<unknown>)
		return not permission.options.hide or permission.can_execute(player, cmd)
	end

	local function update_key(player: Player, state: PlayerState, key: string, changes: NetworkedMap)
		local cmd = registry[key]
		local now = if cmd ~= nil and is_visible(player, cmd) then cmd else nil

		if state.visible[key] ~= now then
			state.visible[key] = now
			changes[key] = if now then get_serialized(now) else { kind = "none" }
		end
	end

	local function add_player(player: Player): PlayerState
		local existing = players[player]
		if existing then
			return existing
		end

		local state: PlayerState
		state = {
			visible = {},
			hydrated = false,
			dirty = false,
			disconnect = permission.on_roles_changed(player, function()
				state.dirty = true
			end),
		}
		players[player] = state
		return state
	end

	local function remove_player(player: Player)
		local state = players[player]
		if state then
			state.disconnect()
			players[player] = nil
		end
	end

	local function hydrate(player: Player)
		assert(send, "connect() must be called before hydrate()")

		local state = players[player]
		if not state then
			if player.Parent ~= services.Players then
				return
			end
			state = add_player(player)
		end

		state.hydrated = true
		state.dirty = false
		state.visible = {}

		local data = {}
		for key, cmd in registry do
			if is_visible(player, cmd) then
				state.visible[key] = cmd
				data[key] = get_serialized(cmd)
			end
		end

		send(
			player,
			{
				type = "init",
				data = data,
			} :: SyncPayload
		)
	end

	local function connect(callback: SyncCallback)
		send = callback
		registry = table.clone(command.commands)

		local disconnect_register = command.on_register(function()
			registry_dirty = true
		end)

		local disconnect_unregister = command.on_unregister(function()
			registry_dirty = true
		end)

		local disconnect_options = permission.on_options_changed(function()
			options_dirty = true
		end)

		-- an edited role can be held directly, inherited or a default role, so
		-- everyone is rechecked like an options change
		local disconnect_role = permission.on_role_updated(function()
			options_dirty = true
		end)

		local heartbeat = services.RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
			-- the registry is diffed once, and each player then only rechecks
			-- the keys that changed. a player whose roles changed, or everyone
			-- when the permission options change, is rechecked in full
			local changed_keys: { [string]: true } = {}
			if registry_dirty then
				for key, cmd in registry do
					if command.commands[key] ~= cmd then
						changed_keys[key] = true
					end
				end
				for key, cmd in command.commands do
					if registry[key] ~= cmd then
						changed_keys[key] = true
					end
				end
				registry = table.clone(command.commands)
			end

			local recheck_all = options_dirty
			registry_dirty = false
			options_dirty = false

			if next(changed_keys) == nil and not recheck_all then
				local any_dirty = false
				for _, state in players do
					if state.dirty then
						any_dirty = true
						break
					end
				end

				if not any_dirty then
					return
				end
			end

			for player, state in players do
				local full = recheck_all or state.dirty
				state.dirty = false

				if not state.hydrated then
					continue
				end

				local changes: NetworkedMap = {}
				if full then
					for key in state.visible do
						if registry[key] == nil then
							update_key(player, state, key, changes)
						end
					end
					for key in registry do
						update_key(player, state, key, changes)
					end
				else
					for key in changed_keys do
						update_key(player, state, key, changes)
					end
				end

				if next(changes) ~= nil then
					callback(
						player,
						{
							type = "patch",
							data = changes,
						} :: SyncPayload
					)
				end
			end
		end)

		local player_added = services.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
			add_player(player)
		end)
		local player_removing = services.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(remove_player)

		for _, player in services.Players:GetPlayers() do
			add_player(player)
		end

		return function()
			disconnect_register()
			disconnect_unregister()
			disconnect_options()
			disconnect_role()
			heartbeat:Disconnect()
			player_added:Disconnect()
			player_removing:Disconnect()

			for player in players do
				remove_player(player)
			end
			send = nil
		end
	end

	return {
		hydrate = hydrate,
		connect = connect,
	}
end

-- whether `input` is the text that `cmd` and `args` were resolved from: its
-- leading unquoted tokens spell the command name and the rest are the
-- arguments, verbatim. the client sends all three, and `input` ends up in
-- `ctx.input`, which guards, listeners and logs read, so it mustn't be able to
-- describe a different command than the one that runs
local function input_matches(cmd: string, args: { string }?, input: string): boolean
	local tokens = parse(input, " ").tokens

	local name_end = 0
	local name = {}
	for i, token in tokens do
		if token.quoted then
			break
		end

		table.insert(name, token.text)
		if table.concat(name, " ") == cmd then
			name_end = i
			break
		end
	end

	if name_end == 0 then
		return false
	end

	local given = args or {}
	if #tokens - name_end ~= #given then
		return false
	end

	for i, arg in given do
		local span = tokens[name_end + i].span
		if input:sub(span.x, span.y) ~= arg then
			return false
		end
	end

	return true
end

local function network_server()
	local syncer = server()

	local server_remotes = require("./network/server")

	local requested: { [Player]: true } = {}
	services.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		requested[player] = nil
	end)

	server_remotes.RequestState.SetCallback(function(player)
		if requested[player] then
			return
		end
		requested[player] = true
		syncer.hydrate(player)
	end)

	syncer.connect(function(player, payload)
		server_remotes.SyncState.Fire(player, payload :: any)
	end)

	server_remotes.Execute.SetCallback(function(player, cmd, args, input): types.ExecutionContext
		local err = limit.check(player, cmd, args, input)
		if err then
			-- don't echo the rejected arguments or input back to the client
			local ctx = context(player, if limit.check_name(cmd) then cmd else "", {}, "")
			ctx.error(err)
			return ctx
		end

		-- fall back to the input rebuilt from `cmd` and `args`
		if input and not input_matches(cmd, args, input) then
			log.warn(`Discarded input from {player.Name} that doesn't match command '{cmd}'.`, {
				executor = player,
				command = cmd,
				input = input,
			})
			input = nil
		end

		local ok, value = xpcall(command.execute :: any, log.capture, player, cmd, args, input)
		if ok then
			return value
		end

		local caught: log.CaughtError = value
		log.error(`Failed to execute '{input or cmd}': {caught.message}`, {
			executor = player,
			command = cmd,
			input = input,
			traceback = caught.traceback,
		})

		local ctx = context(player, cmd, args or {}, input)
		ctx.error("Failed to execute command.")
		return ctx
	end)
end

local function network_client()
	local client_remotes = require("./network/client")
	local syncer = client()

	command.set_network_handler(function(cmd, args, input)
		return client_remotes.Execute.Call(cmd, args, input) :: types.ExecutionContext
	end)

	client_remotes.SyncState.SetCallback(function(...)
		syncer.sync(...)
	end)

	client_remotes.RequestState.Fire()
end

local function setup_networking()
	if services.RunService:IsServer() then
		network_server()
	else
		network_client()
	end
end

return {
	client = client,
	server = server,
	setup = setup_networking,
	input_matches = input_matches,
}

local duration = argument.register_type("duration", {
	transform = function(value: string): types.Result<number>
		if value == "0" then
			return result.success(0)
		end

		local total_seconds = 0
		local pos = value:find("[^%s,]")
		while pos do
			local _, last, amount, unit_name = value:find("^(%d*%.?%d+)%s*(%a+)", pos)
			if not last then
				return result.error(`Invalid duration format: {value}`)
			end

			local unit_seconds = unit_name and units[unit_name:lower()]
			if not unit_seconds then
				return result.error(`Invalid duration unit: {unit_name}`)
			end
			total_seconds += (tonumber(amount) :: number) * unit_seconds
			pos = value:find("[^%s,]", last + 1)
		end

		if total_seconds == 0 then
			return result.error(`Invalid duration format: {value}`)
		end

		-- a long enough run of digits overflows to infinity
		if total_seconds == math.huge then
			return result.error(`Duration is too long: {value}`)
		end

		return result.success(total_seconds)
	end,
	suggestions = function(_value: string, _executor: Player): { string }
		return {}
	end,
})

-- and values like "1e999" that overflow to infinity, none of which make sense
-- as command input. NaN in particular passes any range check, since every
-- comparison with it is false
local function finite(text: string): number?
	local num = tonumber(text)
	if num == nil or num ~= num or num == math.huge or num == -math.huge then
		return nil
	end
	return num
end

local arg_types: { [string]: types.ArgumentType<unknown> } = {}

-- the declarator returns an `Argument`, but it is typed as the transformed
-- value so that a command's `arguments()` tuple types its callback parameters
local function declarator<T, O>(type_name: string): types.ArgumentFn<T, O>
	local function create(
		name: string,
		description: string?,
		suggestions: types.SuggestionList?,
		options: O?
	): types.Argument<O>
		return {
			name = name,
			description = description,
			type = type_name,
			optional = false,
			suggestions = suggestions,
			options = options,
		}
	end

	return (create :: any) :: types.ArgumentFn<T, O>
end

-- `O` is inferred from the type of `arg` in `transform`
local function register_type<T, O>(
	type_name: string,
	data: {
		transform: (text: string, executor: Player, arg: types.Argument<O>) -> types.Result<T>,
		suggestions: ((text: string, executor: Player, arg: types.Argument<O>) -> types.SuggestionList)?,
		check: ((text: string, executor: Player, arg: types.Argument<O>) -> string?)?,
	}
): types.ArgumentFn<T, O>
	assert(arg_types[type_name] == nil, `Argument type '{type_name}' is already registered.`)

	arg_types[type_name] = {
		kind = "single",
		transform = data.transform,
		suggestions = data.suggestions,
		check = data.check,
	} :: any

	return declarator(type_name)
end

local function register_list_type<T, O>(
	type_name: string,
	data: {
		transform: (text: { string }, executor: Player, arg: types.Argument<O>) -> types.Result<T>,
		suggestions: ((text: string, executor: Player, arg: types.Argument<O>) -> types.SuggestionList)?,
		check: ((text: { string }, executor: Player, arg: types.Argument<O>) -> string?)?,
	}
): types.ArgumentFn<T, O>
	assert(arg_types[type_name] == nil, `Argument type '{type_name}' is already registered.`)

	arg_types[type_name] = {
		kind = "list",
		transform = data.transform,
		suggestions = data.suggestions,
		check = data.check,
	} :: any

	return declarator(type_name)
end

local function enum(values: { string })
	local transform = function(value: string): types.Result<string>
		if not table.find(values, value) then
			return result.error(`'{value}' is not a valid option`)
		end
		return result.success(value)
	end

	local suggestions = function()
		return values
	end

	return {
		transform = transform,
		suggestions = suggestions,
	}
end

-- `num_args` and `rest` are typed as `{ T }` so the callback receives an array.
-- that holds at runtime because any argument with `num_args` set, even to 1, is
-- passed as an array; only arguments without it are passed as a single value
local function num_args<T>(argument: T, num: number): { T }
	local arg = table.clone(argument :: types.Argument)
	arg.num_args = num
	return arg :: { T }
end

local function rest<T>(argument: T): { T }
	local arg = table.clone(argument :: types.Argument)
	arg.num_args = "rest"
	return arg :: { T }
end

local function optional<T>(argument: T): T | nil
	local arg = table.clone(argument :: types.Argument)
	arg.optional = true
	return arg
end

export type ArgumentRange = {
	first: number,
	last: number,
}

local function assign(args: { types.Argument }, count: number): ({ ArgumentRange }, number)
	local ranges: { ArgumentRange } = {}

	local index = 1
	for i, arg in args do
		local n_args = arg.num_args or 1
		local last = math.min(if n_args == "rest" then count else index + n_args - 1, count)

		ranges[i] = { first = index, last = last }
		index = math.max(index, last + 1)
	end

	return ranges, index
end

-- when `checking`, a type's `check` is used instead of its `transform` if it has
-- one, and the value is nil
local function value_of(executor: Player, arg: types.Argument, raw: string, checking: boolean): types.Result<unknown>
	local arg_type = arg_types[arg.type]
	assert(arg_type, `Argument type '{arg.type}' is not registered`)

	local parsed_text = {}
	for _, token in parse(raw, arg_type.kind == "single" and " " or ",").tokens do
		table.insert(parsed_text, token.text)
	end

	-- the text matches the type's kind, which the union of function types hides
	local text: any = if arg_type.kind == "single" then parsed_text[1] or "" else parsed_text
	local type_data: any = arg_type
	local check: ((any, Player, types.Argument) -> string?)? = if checking then type_data.check else nil
	if check then
		local err = check(text, executor, arg)
		return if err then result.error(err) else result.success(nil)
	end

	return type_data.transform(text, executor, arg)
end

local function transform_value(executor: Player, arg: types.Argument, raw: string): types.Result<unknown>
	return value_of(executor, arg, raw, false)
end

local function check_value(executor: Player, arg: types.Argument, raw: string): types.Result<unknown>
	return value_of(executor, arg, raw, true)
end

local function run(
	executor: Player,
	input: { string },
	args: { types.Argument },
	checking: boolean
): types.Result<{ unknown }>
	local transformed_args: { unknown } = {}
	local ranges, next_index = assign(args, #input)

	for i, arg in args do
		local n_args = arg.num_args or 1
		local range = ranges[i]
		local count = range.last - range.first + 1

		if count <= 0 then
			if arg.optional then
				continue
			end

			return result.error(`Missing required argument: {arg.name}`)
		end

		local values: { unknown } = {}
		for j = range.first, range.last do
			local res = value_of(executor, arg, input[j], checking)
			if not res.success then
				local at = if count > 1 then ` #{j - range.first + 1}` else ""
				return result.error(`Invalid value{at} for '{arg.name}': {res.error}`)
			end
			values[j - range.first + 1] = res.value
		end

		if type(n_args) == "number" and count ~= n_args then
			return result.error(`Expected {n_args} {n_args == 1 and "value" or "values"} for '{arg.name}', got {count}`)
		end

		if arg.num_args == nil then
			transformed_args[i] = values[1]
		else
			transformed_args[i] = values
		end
	end

	if next_index <= #input then
		local expected = next_index - 1
		if expected == 0 then
			return result.error(`Expected no arguments, got {#input}`)
		end

		return result.error(`Expected at most {expected} {expected == 1 and "argument" or "arguments"}, got {#input}`)
	end

	return result.success(transformed_args)
end

local function transform(executor: Player, input: { string }, args: { types.Argument }): types.Result<{ unknown }>
	return run(executor, input, args, false)
end

-- like `transform`, but cheap enough to run while typing
local function check(executor: Player, input: { string }, args: { types.Argument }): types.Result<{ unknown }>
	return run(executor, input, args, true)
end

return {
	register_type = register_type,
	register_list_type = register_list_type,
	enum = enum,
	optional = optional,
	num_args = num_args,
	rest = rest,
	assign = assign,
	transform_value = transform_value,
	check_value = check_value,
	transform = transform,
	check = check,
	types = arg_types,
}

local argument = require("./.")
local player = require("./player")

local services = require("../services")
local types = require("../types")

export type UserInfo = {
	id: number,
	name: string,
	player: Player?,
}

local function from_player(p: Player): UserInfo
	return { id = p.UserId, name = p.Name, player = p }
end

local function is_me(text: string): boolean
	local lower = text:lower()
	return lower == "@me" or lower == "."
end

-- `#` followed by a user ID
local function parse_id(text: string): number?
	local digits = text:match("^#(%d+)$")
	local id = if digits then tonumber(digits) else nil
	return if id and id > 0 then id else nil
end

local function is_username(text: string): boolean
	return #text >= 3 and #text <= 20 and text:match("^[%w_]+$") ~= nil
end

-- doesn't look anything up, so it can't tell whether the user exists
local function check(text: string): string?
	if is_me(text) or parse_id(text) or is_username(text) then
		return nil
	end
	return `'{text}' is not a valid username or #id.`
end

local function by_id(id: number): types.Result<UserInfo>
	local online = services.Players:GetPlayerByUserId(id)
	if online then
		return result.success(from_player(online))
	end

	local ok, name = pcall(services.Players.GetNameFromUserIdAsync, services.Players, id)
	if not ok then
		return result.error(`User #{id} not found.`)
	end
	local user: UserInfo = { id = id, name = name }
	return result.success(user)
end

-- online players are matched by exact username without a lookup. anyone else
-- is looked up, which yields
local function find_user(text: string, executor: Player): types.Result<UserInfo>
	local err = check(text)
	if err then
		return result.error(err)
	end

	if is_me(text) then
		return result.success(from_player(executor))
	end

	local id = parse_id(text)
	if id then
		return by_id(id)
	end

	local lower = text:lower()
	for _, p in services.Players:GetPlayers() do
		if p.Name:lower() == lower then
			return result.success(from_player(p))

local centurion = require(script.Parent)
local command = require(script.Parent.command)
local types = require("./types")

local CLASS_MARKER = {}

type Guard = string | types.Guard

type CommandOptions = {
	name: (string | { string })?,
	description: string?,
	arguments: (() -> { types.Argument })?,
	guards: { Guard }?,
	roles: { string }?,
	permissions: { string }?,
}

type Metadata = {
	commands: { [string]: CommandOptions },
	groups: { [string | {}]: { string } },
	guards: { [string | {}]: { Guard } },
	roles: { [string | {}]: { string } },
	permissions: { [string | {}]: { string } },
}

local metadata: { [any]: Metadata } = {}

local function get_metadata(target: { [any]: unknown }): Metadata
	if not metadata[target] then
		metadata[target] = {
			commands = {},
			groups = {},
			guards = {},
			roles = {},
			permissions = {},
		}
	end
	return metadata[target]
end

local function collect_metadata(key: string, class_data: { [any]: { any } }, cmd_data: any?)
	local data = table.clone(cmd_data or {}) :: { any }
	if class_data[CLASS_MARKER] then
		for i, v in class_data[CLASS_MARKER] do
			table.insert(data, i, v)
		end
	end

	if class_data[key] then
		for _, v in class_data[key] do
			table.insert(data, v)
		end
	end

	return data
end

local function command_decorator(options: CommandOptions)
	return function(target: { [any]: unknown }, key: string)
		get_metadata(target).commands[key] = options
	end
end

local function group_decorator(...: string)
	local group = { ... }

	return function(target: { [any]: unknown }, key: string?)
		get_metadata(target).groups[key or CLASS_MARKER] = group
	end
end

local function stack<T>(data: { [string | {}]: { T } }, key: string | {}, values: { T })
	local existing = data[key]
	if existing then
		table.move(existing, 1, #existing, #values + 1, values)
	end
	data[key] = values
end

local function guard_decorator(...: Guard)
	local guards = { ... }

	return function(target: { [any]: unknown }, key: string?)
		stack(get_metadata(target).guards, key or CLASS_MARKER, table.clone(guards))
	end
end

local function role_decorator(...: string)
	local roles = { ... }

	return function(target: { [any]: unknown }, key: string?)
		stack(get_metadata(target).roles, key or CLASS_MARKER, table.clone(roles))
	end
end

local function permission_decorator(...: string)
	local permissions = { ... }

	return function(target: { [any]: unknown }, key: string?)
		stack(get_metadata(target).permissions, key or CLASS_MARKER, table.clone(permissions))
	end
end

local function register_classes(constructor)
	for class, class_metadata in metadata do
		if next(class_metadata.commands) == nil then
			continue
		end

		local instance: { [any]: unknown }
		if constructor then
			instance = constructor(class)
			assert(type(instance) == "table", "Constructor function must return an object")
		else
			instance = setmetatable({}, class) :: { constructor: (unknown) -> any, [any]: unknown }
			instance:constructor()
		end

		local class_group = class_metadata.groups[CLASS_MARKER]

		for key, cmd in class_metadata.commands do
			local cmd_groups = if class_group then table.clone(class_group) else {}
			if class_metadata.groups[key] then
				for _, group in class_metadata.groups[key] do
					table.insert(cmd_groups, group)
				end
			end

			local cmd_name = cmd.name or key
			if type(cmd_name) == "string" then
				cmd_name = { cmd_name }
			else
				cmd_name = table.clone(cmd_name)
			end

			if #cmd_groups > 0 then
				local group_prefix = table.concat(cmd_groups, " ")
				for i, name in cmd_name :: { string } do
					(cmd_name :: { string })[i] = group_prefix .. " " .. name
				end
			end

			local args = cmd.arguments

			command.check_arity((cmd_name :: { string })[1], (instance :: any)[key], args and #args() or 0, 2)

			centurion.register_command(
				cmd_name,
				{
					callback = function(ctx: types.ExecutionContext, ...)
						return (instance :: any)[key](instance, ctx, ...)
					end,
					description = cmd.description,
					arguments = args and function()
						return table.unpack(args() :: any)
					end or nil,
					guards = collect_metadata(key, class_metadata.guards, cmd.guards),
					roles = collect_metadata(key, class_metadata.roles, cmd.roles),
					permissions = collect_metadata(key, class_metadata.permissions, cmd.permissions),
				} :: types.Command<unknown>
			)
		end
	end
	table.clear(metadata)
end

local function register_command<T...>(name: string, command_object: types.Command<T...>)
	local cmd = table.clone(command_object) :: any

	local args = command_object.arguments
	if args then
		cmd.arguments = function()
			return table.unpack(args() :: any)
		end
	end
	centurion.register_command(name, cmd :: types.Command<unknown>)
end

	Role = role_decorator,

	register_classes = register_classes,
	register_command = register_command,
}
